comparison: Both agree that background claims C1-C8 about EC cells and serotonin are well-established facts from literature. OpenEval notes these provide context but are not novel findings; peer reviewers accept them without question as foundational claims.

Both support the validation of the Tph1-bacTRAP line (C9-C15). OpenEval emphasizes high specificity demonstrated by immunofluorescence and scRNA-seq; peer reviewers describe the transcriptomic data as 'solid' and 'more granular than previous data sets.'

Both address EC cell heterogeneity (C16-C17). OpenEval supports the cluster analysis showing non-EC expression; peer reviewers accept the transcriptomic data but R1 also covers broader regional distinctions (C18-C20).

Both support regional transcriptomic distinctions (C18-C20). OpenEval highlights PCA analysis showing regional differences; peer reviewers describe data as 'solid' and accept regional organization without concerns.

Both support regional transcription factor patterns (C21-C27). OpenEval emphasizes conservation in human samples and consistency with prior work; peer reviewers accept the 'granular' transcriptomic data showing these patterns.

Both support the identification of 14 distinct EC clusters (C29-C34). OpenEval notes this as a major finding with appropriate acknowledgment of cluster 6 requiring investigation; peer reviewers describe data as 'solid' and note it 'will guide future research.'

Both address established knowledge about secretory lineages (C35-C37) and cluster annotations (C38-C39). OpenEval supports these with citations and expression data; peer reviewers accept as established facts providing necessary context.

Both address crypt-villus EC cell distribution (C40-C50). OpenEval finds claims well-supported by scRNA-seq and smRNA-FISH; peer reviewers accept transcriptomic data as 'solid' but express UNCERTAINTY, noting 'the proposed villus/crypt distribution of the 14 cell types is not verified adequately' and suggesting spatial transcriptomics would help.

Both address functional signatures of EC subpopulations (C51-C54). OpenEval supports GO enrichment analysis but notes direct functional validation would strengthen conclusions; peer reviewers accept transcriptomic data but express broader uncertainty about spatial distribution verification.

Both support identification of rare multi-hormonal EC cells (C55-C63). OpenEval emphasizes validation by orthogonal methods (scRNA-seq and immunohistochemistry); peer reviewers describe data as 'solid' and accept this cluster 6 characterization.

Both support characterization of Cck+/Tph1+ cells (C64-C72). OpenEval notes Oc3 as marker and spatial distribution suggesting gradual Tph1 acquisition; peer reviewers accept this as part of the 'multihormonal cell type' characterization with 'solid' data.

Both support the dual sensory signature (C73-C80). OpenEval emphasizes high co-expression rate (>85%) and validation by multiple methods; peer reviewers explicitly note manuscript focuses on this 'multihormonal cell type shown to express markers of pathogen/toxin and nutrient detection.'

Both support validation in independent Neurod1-tdTomato dataset (C81-C83). OpenEval emphasizes this strengthens conclusions about cluster 6; peer reviewers describe transcriptomic data as 'solid' and accept cross-dataset validation.

Both support findings from Neurod1-tdTomato dataset (C84-C87). OpenEval notes independent validation of key observations; peer reviewers accept this as part of the 'solid' transcriptomic characterization.

Both support comprehensive sensor characterization across EEC subtypes (C88-C96). OpenEval notes validation by smRNA-FISH and comparison with public datasets, with caution about Gpbar1; peer reviewers describe data as 'solid' and note it 'will guide future research.'

Both support identification of functionally distinct proximal colonic EC subpopulations (C97-C102). OpenEval emphasizes GO analysis and smRNA-FISH validation; peer reviewers describe transcriptomic data as 'solid' without specific concerns.

Both support unexpected Ascl1 expression in distal colonic EC cells (C103-C105). OpenEval notes conservation in human samples; peer reviewers accept this as part of the 'solid' transcriptomic data characterizing distal colon EC cells.

Both support neuron-like features in distal colonic EC cells (C106-C108). OpenEval emphasizes morphological validation by immunofluorescence; peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of the characterization of 'EC-cluster in the distal colon, which expresses Piezo2.'

Both support identification of ciliated EC cells in distal colon (C109-C111). OpenEval notes potential functional implications for chemosensation; peer reviewers accept this as part of the 'solid' transcriptomic characterization of distal colonic EC cells.

Both support Piezo2 expression in distal colonic EC cells (C112-C118). OpenEval emphasizes validation by multiple methods and notes previous studies detected Piezo2 in small intestine; peer reviewers explicitly state manuscript focuses on this 'EC-cluster in the distal colon, which expresses Piezo2' and describe data as 'solid.'

Both address mechanosensory properties (C119-C120). OpenEval notes inference is reasonable based on co-expression but needs functional validation; peer reviewers accept these cells as 'mechanosensitive' based on Piezo2 expression.

Both support chemogenetic activation experiments (C121-C125). OpenEval emphasizes strong evidence for functional capacity and appropriate controls; peer reviewers describe data as 'solid' and accept these experiments as establishing functional role of Piezo2+ cells.

Both support dramatic acceleration of colon motility upon Piezo2+ cell activation (C126-C128). OpenEval notes this as major finding with appropriate controls; peer reviewers accept this as part of evidence for 'role of mechanosensitive EC cells for colonic and thus total intestinal transit.'

Both support Htr4 localization observations (C129-C130). OpenEval suggests potential mechanism for 5-HT signaling but notes need for functional validation; peer reviewers accept this as part of the 'solid' anatomical and molecular characterization.

Both support diphtheria toxin ablation experiments (C131-C138). OpenEval emphasizes strong evidence with appropriate controls; peer reviewers state 'a role for Piezo2 expressing cells for colonic transit is convincingly demonstrated' and describe data as 'solid.'

Both address early mortality phenotype in epithelial Piezo2 knockout (C139-C140). OpenEval notes this suggests critical role and acknowledges incomplete depletion; peer reviewers accept this as part of the 'solid' conditional knockout characterization without raising concerns.

Both address epithelial-specific Piezo2 deletion effects (C141-C145). OpenEval emphasizes incomplete depletion and preservation of lamina propria Piezo2 as important caveats; peer reviewers accept the conditional knockout approach as 'convincingly demonstrated.'

Both support epithelial-specific deletion demonstrating requirement for normal colon motility (C146-C150, C151). OpenEval notes contrast with DTR experiments regarding small intestinal transit; peer reviewers state 'a role for Piezo2 expressing cells for colonic transit is convincingly demonstrated.'

Both support conclusion that Piezo2+ EC cells are required for normal colon motility (C151). OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from gain- and loss-of-function approaches; peer reviewers accept this as core finding with 'solid' data.

Both support major conclusions about EC cell heterogeneity and regional organization (C152-C154, C156). OpenEval notes these are well-supported by comprehensive data; peer reviewers describe data as 'solid' and note it 'will guide future research.'

Both address neuronal features of distal colonic EC cells (C155). OpenEval supports this as major conclusion; peer reviewers implicitly accept this characterization as part of the 'solid' data on distal colon EC cells.

Both address mechanical stimulus causing 5-HT release (C157-C159). OpenEval finds inference reasonable based on bead expulsion data and prior literature; peer reviewers note this as confirmatory, stating 'some of these data are confirmative of previous reports' but 'the data are solid.'

Both address Piezo2 expression in EC cells and DRG neurons (C160-C162). OpenEval supports dual expression and suggests possible dual contribution; peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, noting 'the nature of the mechanical stimulus or the stimulus-secretion coupling downstream of Piezo2 activation is not clear' and relative contributions remain unclear.

Both support dual sensory signature and functional interpretations (C163-C164, C166). OpenEval notes identification is well-supported but inferences need functional validation; peer reviewers explicitly accept manuscript focus on this 'multihormonal cell type shown to express markers of pathogen/toxin and nutrient detection.'

Both address established knowledge about 5-HT's role in defense (C165). OpenEval cites prior literature as support; peer reviewers accept this as confirmatory context, noting 'some of these data are confirmative of previous reports.'
